root_cause_label: Constraint Misinterpretation Leading to Root Directory Item Limit Violation
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent misinterpreted the 30-item directory constraint as a per-file record limit, causing compress.py to place all 396 resharded subdirectories directly in the output root (far exceeding the 30-item cap), while the decompress.py script also failed to remove resharded artifacts after restoring original files.
t_err_evidence: Agent creates compress.py without metadata tracking needed for faithful decompression.
t_commit_evidence: Step 11: The agent executes `python /app/compress.py /app/c4_sample /app/test_compressed` on the full 9,898-file dataset, creating the flawed 396-subdirectory structure. After this execution the violating layout is locked in; the agent never revisits the root-directory item count in all subsequent steps.
t_surface_evidence: find /app/test_compressed -name 'reshard_*' | wc -l returns 396, far exceeding 30-dir limit.
trigger_explanation: The agent wrote compress.py under the false premise that the '30 files or folders per directory' constraint meant 30 JSON records per output file, not that each directory (including the output root) may contain at most 30 entries. This unverified assumption was never checked against the actual task specification before writing and executing the script.
